sections.heading: How did Fenerbahçe get to this round?
paragraphs: In the second qualifying round, Fenerbahçe knocked out the Polish side Górnik Zabrze 2-1 on aggregate. The first leg in Kadıköy ended 1-0, and in the second leg in Poland the yellow-and-navy side went ahead through an Anderson Talisca penalty, left the pitch with a 1-1 draw and secured a place in the third round. The team began preparing for Sturm Graz on 30 July.

sections.heading: Opposition analysis: what kind of side are Sturm Graz?
paragraphs: In the second qualifying round, Sturm Graz knocked out the Scottish side Hearts, beating them 4-0 in the first leg and 2-0 away in the second, 6-0 on aggregate. Scoring six goals in two matches without conceding, the Austrian side's form in the qualifying run makes them the side in this tie that has to be taken seriously.

FutbolRadar's view: for a Fenerbahçe side that managed two goals over two matches against Górnik, turning a score advantage in Kadıköy into a different result is the most important factor in easing the pressure of the second leg in Graz.

The press claims that a two-year package of €17 million a year plus bonuses was offered; Trabzonspor President Ertuğrul Doğan said on 2 August, 'there is no such agreement at the moment'. claims.statement: It was claimed that Trabzonspor offered Salah €17 million a year plus bonuses for two years.
Ertuğrul Doğan: 'There is no such agreement at the moment. I did not say the process is continuing.'

sections.heading: What do we know, and what do we not?
paragraphs: Known: in his 2 August statement, Trabzonspor President Ertuğrul Doğan did not confirm claims that an agreement for Salah exists, and did not confirm the reports that the player will come to Trabzon. This is the only official statement from the club side in the file.

Unknown: whether an offer exists, its amount and the stage of the talks. The '€17 million a year plus bonuses' figure circulating in the press has not been confirmed by any party. FutbolRadar relays these figures as claims; it does not present them as confirmed information.

sections.heading: How should the likelihood of it happening be read?
paragraphs: In the file's current state, giving a numerical assessment of the likelihood would be speculation; the club president's public denial shows that the claims are at least not at the 'agreement' stage. Signs to watch: Trabzonspor's official channels, a clear message from the player's side, and primary-source confirmation in the European press.

The dynamics of the transfer window also matter: the summer window in Europe's major leagues closes in early September. The file could become clear in either direction by then; this page will be updated at every significant development.

faq.a: No. As of 3 August 2026 there is no confirmed agreement or signature; the club president denied the claims of an agreement.

avrupa-ligi-eleme-sistemi-rehberi.title: UEFA Europa League Qualifying System: How the Rounds and League Phase Work | FutbolRadar
avrupa-ligi-eleme-sistemi-rehberi.description: A guide to the UEFA Europa League qualifying system: how the qualifying rounds, the play-off and the 36-team league phase work, using Beşiktaş's route as the example.
avrupa-ligi-eleme-sistemi-rehberi.h1: How does the UEFA Europa League qualifying system work?
avrupa-ligi-eleme-sistemi-rehberi.directAnswer: Entry to the UEFA Europa League begins with qualifying rounds played through the summer: teams progress through successive two-legged rounds, and those who win the final step, the play-off round, join the 36-team league phase. In the league phase each team plays 8 matches; the top 8 go straight to the round of 16, and teams in positions 9-24 play a two-legged play-off.

sections.heading: Qualifying rounds: two-legged ties
paragraphs: The road to the Europa League runs through qualifying rounds played in July and August. Each tie is played over two matches, home and away, and the side ahead on aggregate goes through. If it is level, extra time follows and, if needed, a penalty shoot-out. In 2026-27 Beşiktaş joined this route in the second qualifying round: the black-and-whites knocked out Midtjylland and were drawn against Hradec Králové in the third qualifying round.

The teams that win the third qualifying round move up to the play-off round, the last step before the league phase. The play-off is also played over two legs; the winners join the Europa League's main stage, the league phase.

sections.heading: League phase: 36 teams, 8 matches
paragraphs: With the format introduced in 2024, a single league table replaced the group stage: 36 teams each play 8 different opponents decided by the draw (4 at home, 4 away), and all teams are ranked in the same table.

The teams that finish the league phase in the top 8 go straight to the round of 16. The 16 teams in positions 9 to 24 play a two-legged knockout play-off before the round of 16. Teams in 25th place and below leave Europe; there is no drop down to another competition.

What the top 8 get - going straight to the round of 16, skipping the knockout play-off and being seeded - is covered on the page [what happens when you finish in the top 8](en/guides/europa-league-top-8-rule.html).

sections.heading: Which competition do eliminated teams go to?
paragraphs: Losing on the qualifying route is not always the end of Europe: some teams knocked out in the qualifying rounds and the play-off are redirected to the corresponding step of the Conference League according to UEFA's access list. Which round leads to which competition is set in the season's access list; we announce confirmed redirections separately in matchweeks.

FutbolRadar's view: the format turns August into a demanding test for teams coming through the qualifying route - as in Beşiktaş's case, the league opener and the European second legs are squeezed into the same week. Squad depth matters more in this period than the classic 'first XI' debate.

faq.q: Is there a group stage in the Europa League?
faq.a: No; since 2024 a single 36-team league table has been played. Each team plays 8 matches.

faq.q: What does finishing in the top 8 of the league phase earn?
faq.a: The top 8 go straight to the round of 16; positions 9-24 play a two-legged play-off.

faq.q: Which round is Beşiktaş in?
faq.a: Beşiktaş were drawn against Hradec Králové in the 3rd qualifying round; the first leg is on 6 August in Czechia.

besiktas-yeni-transferleri-2026-2027.title: Beşiktaş's New Signings 2026-27: Arrivals, Departures and the Rumour Mill | FutbolRadar
besiktas-yeni-transferleri-2026-2027.description: Beşiktaş's 7 confirmed 2026-27 signings (including Trossard, Nübel, Vlahovic, Poku and Miretti), departures and the press target list on one page, with claims kept apart from confirmations.
besiktas-yeni-transferleri-2026-2027.h1: Beşiktaş's 2026-27 transfers: arrivals, departures and the rumour mill
besiktas-yeni-transferleri-2026-2027.directAnswer: Beşiktaş's confirmed transfers for the 2026-27 season: Leandro Trossard (from Arsenal on a permanent transfer), Alexander Nübel (from Bayern Munich), Salih Özcan (free agent), Doğan Alemdar (from Başakşehir), Dusan Vlahovic (as a free agent), Ernest Poku (on loan from Bayer Leverkusen) and Fabio Miretti (on loan from Juventus). Tayyip Talha Sanuç left for Çaykur Rizespor on a permanent transfer. The Patrick Schick and Darwin Núñez headlines in the press are unconfirmed items; the Mohamed Salah file ended with his official transfer to Trabzonspor.
besiktas-yeni-transferleri-2026-2027.updateNote: The table is updated as new official announcements arrive; unconfirmed names stay in the 'rumour mill' section.

sections.heading: Confirmed arrivals
paragraphs: Seven signings are settled through club announcements: Leandro Trossard joined from Arsenal on a permanent transfer on 15 July; Alexander Nübel came from Bayern Munich for the goal, free agent Salih Özcan for midfield, and Doğan Alemdar from Başakşehir for squad depth. The centre-forward line was strengthened on 13 August with free agent Dusan Vlahovic.

Two moves at the end of August widened the squad: Ernest Poku on loan from Bayer Leverkusen (with an option to buy) was officially announced on 27 August, and Fabio Miretti on loan from Juventus (with an option to buy) on 28 August.
On the departures side, the clearest deal is in defence: Tayyip Talha Sanuç left for Çaykur Rizespor on a permanent transfer on 19 July.

sections.heading: The press agenda: unconfirmed headlines
paragraphs: Two names are still circulating in the press on the centre-forward route: it is written that talks continue for Bayer Leverkusen striker Patrick Schick, with the club working on a payment plan against a €25 million asking price; for Darwin Núñez, who left Al Hilal, sources including Fabrizio Romano say there is not yet an agreement with Beşiktaş and that the player is weighing several offers. Neither headline has been confirmed by the club.

The Mohamed Salah file, which was earlier tracked on this page with 'rumour' status, is closed: the player officially transferred to Trabzonspor on 6 August, and the Beşiktaş link did not materialise.

FutbolRadar's view: with the Vlahovic, Poku and Miretti signings, attacking and midfield depth has clearly increased; a second centre-forward (Schick) remains an open file, but it is now a rotation debate rather than a necessity. Whether these two headlines are resolved before the transfer window closes on 4 September will be watched.

faq.q: Who has Beşiktaş signed this season?
faq.a: Confirmed signings: Leandro Trossard, Alexander Nübel, Salih Özcan, Doğan Alemdar, Dusan Vlahovic, Ernest Poku and Fabio Miretti.

faq.q: Who has left Beşiktaş?
faq.a: Tayyip Talha Sanuç left for Çaykur Rizespor on a permanent transfer.

faq.q: Are the Vlahovic and Salah transfers done?
faq.a: Vlahovic, yes: he joined Beşiktaş as a free agent on 13 August. Salah did not join Beşiktaş; he officially transferred to Trabzonspor on 6 August.

faq.q: Are the Schick and Núñez transfers done?
faq.a: No; both are among the unconfirmed items in the press and have not been confirmed by the club.

avrupa-ligi-ilk-8-kurali.title: What Happens When You Finish in the Europa League Top 8? Round of 16 and Seeding | FutbolRadar
avrupa-ligi-ilk-8-kurali.description: The top 8 go straight to the round of 16 and skip the knockout play-off. In the round of 16 draw they are seeded and, as a rule, play the second leg at home.
avrupa-ligi-ilk-8-kurali.h1: What happens when a team finishes in the Europa League top 8?
avrupa-ligi-ilk-8-kurali.directAnswer: A team that finishes the league phase in the top 8 goes straight to the round of 16 and does not play the knockout play-off after the league phase. In the round of 16 draw it is seeded and, as a rule, plays the second leg at home. The qualifying rounds and the whole league phase are covered on the page [all the Europa League rules](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-system-guide.html).

sections.heading: Straight to the round of 16, exempt from the knockout play-off
paragraphs: Article 17.04 of the 2026/27 UEFA Europa League Regulations splits the standings into three when the league phase ends. Clubs in positions 1 to 8 advance to the round of 16. Clubs in positions 9 to 24 go into the knockout play-off. The top 8 do not appear in the pairings of that knockout play-off.

The same article treats positions 25 to 36 as eliminated. This page does not describe what happens to those positions; it describes the place in the next round that the top 8 win. How long the league phase lasts and how the qualifying rounds work is on the page [all the Europa League rules](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-system-guide.html).

sections.heading: Being seeded in the round of 16 draw and playing the second leg at home
paragraphs: Article 19.01 says that when the league phase is complete, the 24 clubs entering the knockout phase stand in pre-set positions according to their place in the standings. Article 19.03 sets up the round of 16 draw as follows. Positions 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 7 and 8 form four pairs of seeded clubs. The clubs in each pair are drawn against the relevant one of the knockout play-off winners, into one of the two positions shown in the annex.

A seeded club plays the second leg at home as a rule. Article 19 also states that UEFA's administration may change the draw conditions and assign positions because of restrictions arising from decisions of the Executive Committee. The home second leg therefore stands as the principle of the rule.

sections.heading: The home-advantage that rank brings in the quarter-finals and semi-finals
paragraphs: Article 19.04 says that the clubs that finish the league phase in positions 1 to 4 will, as a rule, play the quarter-final second leg at home. The clubs in positions 1 and 2 also play the semi-final second leg at home as a rule. Positions 5 to 8 are seeded in the round of 16; the article text does not give those positions this extra home advantage in the quarter-finals and semi-finals.

If a seeded club is knocked out, the club that eliminated it takes over that seeded position. The standings are not recalculated after each round. The top 8's advantage stays in its position in the pairing scheme until they are eliminated; once they are, the same position passes to the opponent.

Article 20.01 has knockout ties other than the final played over two matches, home and away. Article 20.03 says that the side ahead on aggregate goals over the two matches goes through to the next round. If aggregate goals are level, Article 21 brings in two 15-minute periods of extra time at the end of the second match and, if needed, a penalty shoot-out.

faq.q: What happens when you finish in the Europa League top 8?
faq.a: The team goes straight to the round of 16 and does not play the knockout play-off after the league phase.

faq.q: Does the top 8 play the knockout play-off?
faq.a: No. The knockout play-off is for positions 9 to 24. The top 8 skip this round.

faq.q: Whose ground is the round of 16 second leg played on?
faq.a: The top 8 are seeded and, as a rule, play the second leg at home. UEFA's administration may change the draw conditions because of restrictions.

faq.q: Do 1st and 8th place get the same advantage?
faq.a: Both are seeded in the round of 16. The right to play the quarter-final second leg at home belongs to positions 1-4, and the right to play the semi-final second leg at home to positions 1 and 2.

avrupa-liginden-elenince-ne-olur.title: What Happens to a Team Knocked Out of the Europa League? Play-off and League Phase | FutbolRadar
avrupa-liginden-elenince-ne-olur.description: A team knocked out in summer qualifying drops into the Conference League according to its round. In the league phase, positions 25-36 are eliminated; those positions are not written into the Conference League.
avrupa-liginden-elenince-ne-olur.h1: What happens to a team knocked out of the Europa League?
avrupa-liginden-elenince-ne-olur.directAnswer: A team knocked out in summer qualifying or in the play-off before the league phase is taken into the corresponding round of the Conference League according to the table in Article 3.06 of the 2026/27 regulations. A team finishing the league phase in 25th-36th place is eliminated; this table contains no row linking those positions to the Conference League. A team that loses the knockout play-off after the league phase cannot reach the round of 16.

sections.heading: Which Conference League round does a team knocked out in qualifying go to?
paragraphs: Article 3.06 shows in a table how clubs knocked out in the Champions League or Europa League qualifying phase and play-off are taken into the Europa League or the Conference League. Article 15.03 says that clubs eliminated from the Champions League from the second qualifying round onward enter the ongoing Europa League according to this table, and that eliminations after the Europa League are likewise linked to the Conference League in the same table.

In the main path section of the table, a team knocked out in the first qualifying round is written into the Conference League second qualifying round, and a team knocked out in the second qualifying round into the Conference League third qualifying round. The Conference League column of the third qualifying round row is the play-off. The play-off row shows the Conference League league phase for both the Champions Path and the main path.

The Champions Path enters the Europa League from the third qualifying round. The transfer to the Conference League in the first and second qualifying rounds belongs to the rows of the main path. The number and calendar of the rounds are on the pages [how many qualifying rounds are there](en/guides/how-many-qualifying-rounds-in-the-europa-league.html) and [when are the qualifying matches](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-dates-2026-27.html), and the whole format is on the page [all the Europa League rules](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-system-guide.html).

sections.heading: 25th place and below in the league phase
paragraphs: Article 17.04 treats clubs finishing the league phase in positions 25 to 36 as eliminated. The transfer table in Article 3.06 covers the qualifying phase and the play-off before the league phase; it carries no Conference League row for the league phase standings.

Positions 1 to 8 going straight to the round of 16 and positions 9 to 24 going to the knockout play-off are the other two rows of the same article. The top 8's seeding and home second leg are explained on the page [what happens when you finish in the top 8](en/guides/europa-league-top-8-rule.html).

sections.heading: A team that loses the play-off after the league phase
paragraphs: Positions 9 to 24 play the knockout play-off after the league phase ends. This round is not the same step as the play-off played in the summer before the league phase. Article 13 counts the summer play-off as a separate step after the qualifying phase, and the knockout play-off as the first step of the knockout phase after the league phase.

Article 20.03 says that the side ahead on aggregate goals over the two matches goes through to the next round. If the aggregate is level, Article 21 brings in extra time and the penalty shoot-out. The losing side cannot reach the round of 16. Article 3.06 does not list this knockout play-off as a row that transfers to the Conference League.

faq.q: What happens to a team knocked out of the Europa League?
faq.a: A team knocked out in summer qualifying or in the play-off before the league phase is taken into the Conference League according to the round in which it went out. In the league phase, positions 25-36 are eliminated.

faq.q: Does a team knocked out in the play-off go to the Conference League?
faq.a: A team knocked out in the play-off before the league phase is written into the Conference League league phase in Article 3.06. A team that loses the knockout play-off after the league phase cannot reach the round of 16; Article 3.06 does not link that round to the Conference League.

faq.q: Where does a team knocked out in the third qualifying round go?
faq.a: In the Article 3.06 table, the Conference League column of the third qualifying round row is the play-off.

faq.q: What happens when the top 8 are knocked out?
faq.a: The top 8 go to the round of 16 without playing the knockout play-off. The draw for this round and the home second leg are on a separate page.

avrupa-ligi-kac-eleme-turu.title: How Many Qualifying Rounds Are There in the Europa League? Preliminary Rounds and Play-off | FutbolRadar
avrupa-ligi-kac-eleme-turu.description: The main path has three qualifying rounds: first, second and third. The Champions Path enters at the third round. A separate play-off follows.
avrupa-ligi-kac-eleme-turu.h1: How many qualifying rounds are there in the Europa League?
avrupa-ligi-kac-eleme-turu.directAnswer: The UEFA Europa League qualifying phase has three rounds on the main path: the first, second and third qualifying rounds. The Champions Path enters only at the third qualifying round. After these rounds, a separate play-off round is played before the league phase. Not every team plays every round.

sections.heading: Main path: three qualifying rounds
paragraphs: Article 13 of the 2026/27 UEFA Europa League Regulations splits the qualifying phase into two paths. The main path consists of the first qualifying round, the second qualifying round and the third qualifying round. These three rounds are what the regulations call the answer to the preliminary-rounds question.

Under Article 15.01, each tie is played over two matches, home and away. The side ahead on the aggregate goals of the two matches goes through to the next round or phase. If the aggregate is level, Article 21 applies. UEFA's administration may reduce a tie to a single match if conditions require, and sets out the principle for deciding the winner separately.

sections.heading: The Champions Path enters only at the third round
paragraphs: The same article defines the Champions Path with a single round: the third qualifying round. A team on the Champions Path does not play the first and second rounds of the Europa League qualifying phase.
Which round a team enters at is based on the country club coefficient ranking, as UEFA states in its 2026/27 season note. Not all clubs play all three qualifying rounds.

sections.heading: The play-off is a separate step outside the three qualifying rounds
paragraphs: Article 13 does not count the play-off as a fourth preliminary round inside the qualifying phase. It writes it as a separate play-off round that follows the qualifying phase and comes before the league phase. The steps ahead of a team until the league phase are, depending on where it enters, at most three qualifying rounds plus this play-off.

The play-off also falls under the two-legged knockout procedure of Article 15. Whether a team knocked out in this round goes to the Conference League is on the page [what happens to a team knocked out](en/guides/what-happens-when-a-team-is-knocked-out-of-the-europa-league.html), the days of the rounds are on the page [when are the qualifying matches](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-dates-2026-27.html), and the whole format is on the page [all the Europa League rules](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-system-guide.html).

faq.q: How many qualifying rounds are there in the Europa League?
faq.a: The main path has three qualifying rounds: first, second and third. A separate play-off round follows.

faq.q: How many preliminary rounds are there?
faq.a: The regulations write the qualifying phase as three rounds on the main path. The Champions Path plays only the third round.

faq.q: Is the play-off a qualifying round?
faq.a: The play-off is a separate step played after the qualifying phase and before the league phase. It is not written into the three preliminary rounds.

faq.q: Does every team play all three rounds?
faq.a: No. The entry round varies with the country's club coefficient. The Champions Path starts at the third round.

avrupa-ligi-eleme-maclari-ne-zaman.title: When Are the UEFA Europa League Qualifying Matches? 2026/27 Calendar | FutbolRadar
avrupa-ligi-eleme-maclari-ne-zaman.description: According to the UEFA calendar, the 2026/27 qualifying matches start on 9 July. The rounds fall on 16 July, 23 and 30 July, 6 and 13 August, and 20 and 27 August.
avrupa-ligi-eleme-maclari-ne-zaman.h1: When are the UEFA Europa League qualifying matches?
avrupa-ligi-eleme-maclari-ne-zaman.directAnswer: According to the UEFA calendar, the 2026/27 Europa League qualifying matches start on 9 July 2026. The first-round second legs are on 16 July, the second round on 23 and 30 July, the third round on 6 and 13 August, and the play-off on 20 and 27 August 2026. UEFA states that these dates are for information and may change.

sections.heading: The 2026/27 qualifying and play-off dates
paragraphs: UEFA's 2026 European football calendar, dated 31 August 2026, gives the Europa League qualifying dates as follows. First qualifying round first legs on 9 July 2026, second legs on 16 July 2026. Second qualifying round first legs on 23 July 2026, second legs on 30 July 2026. Third qualifying round first legs on 6 August 2026, second legs on 13 August 2026. Play-off first legs on 20 August 2026, second legs on 27 August 2026.

UEFA's 16 June 2026 announcement of the first qualifying round draw also gives the first legs as 9 July and the second legs as 16 July. The season page dated 23 November 2026 says that the 2026/27 Europa League began on 9 July 2026 and that the play-off was completed in August. The same page notes that the dates may change.

sections.heading: The first league phase day after qualifying ends
paragraphs: The same UEFA calendar and the 23 November 2026 season page give league phase matchday 1 as 16/17 September 2026. This day is not a qualifying round; it is the official boundary at which the qualifying and play-off calendar ends.

The number of rounds and how many rounds each path plays is on the page [how many qualifying rounds are there](en/guides/how-many-qualifying-rounds-in-the-europa-league.html), where a knocked-out team goes is on the page [what happens to a team knocked out](en/guides/what-happens-when-a-team-is-knocked-out-of-the-europa-league.html), and the whole format is on the page [all the Europa League rules](en/guides/europa-league-qualifying-system-guide.html).

sections.heading: Why the calendar does not give a single kick-off time
paragraphs: The UEFA calendar publishes the days of the rounds; it does not list the kick-off time and stadium of each tie one by one. The days on this page are the published qualifying calendar for the 2026/27 season. Qualifying days for other seasons are not in this list.

The draw dates are in the same calendar: the first qualifying round draw on 16 June, the second qualifying round draw on 17 June, the third qualifying round draw on 20 July, the play-off draw on 3 August, and the league phase draw on 28 August 2026.

faq.q: When are the UEFA Europa League qualifying matches?
faq.a: In 2026/27 the first round is on 9 and 16 July, the second round on 23 and 30 July, the third round on 6 and 13 August, and the play-off on 20 and 27 August 2026.

faq.q: On which days are the play-off matches?
faq.a: The UEFA calendar gives the play-off first legs as 20 August 2026 and the second legs as 27 August 2026.

faq.q: Are the dates final?
faq.a: The UEFA calendar is for information and states that dates may change. The days here are taken from that published calendar.

faq.q: How many qualifying rounds are played?
faq.a: There are three qualifying rounds on the main path, followed by a separate play-off. The definition of the rounds is on a separate page.

super-lig-kume-dusme-ve-averaj.title: How Do Relegation and Tiebreakers Work in the Süper Lig? | FutbolRadar
super-lig-kume-dusme-ve-averaj.description: In the 2026-2027 Süper Lig, the three teams in 16th, 17th and 18th place are relegated to the 1. Lig. When points are level, the TFF looks first at the matches between the teams themselves.
super-lig-kume-dusme-ve-averaj.h1: How do relegation and tiebreakers work in the Süper Lig?
super-lig-kume-dusme-ve-averaj.directAnswer: Under the 2026-2027 Süper Lig Competition Statute, the three teams in 16th, 17th and 18th place at the end of the season are relegated to the TFF 1. Lig. When points are level, the order is decided under Article 9 of the Football Match Instruction first by the matches between the teams themselves. Overall goal difference comes after that order.

sections.heading: The bottom three go down to the TFF 1. Lig
paragraphs: Article 3 of the 2026-2027 Süper Lig Competition Statute has the league played among 18 teams in a double round-robin. The second paragraph of the same article says that the three teams finishing 16th, 17th and 18th at the end of the season are relegated to the TFF 1. Lig.

The Statute was adopted at the TFF Board meeting no. 72 of 14.05.2026 and entered into force when it was published at tff.org on 21.05.2026. Meeting no. 79 of 30.07.2026 amended the first paragraph of Article 10. Article 3, which sets out relegation, is not mentioned in that amendment text.
The current order is on the page [Süper Lig standings](en/super-lig-standings.html). This page does not describe today's places in that table; it describes the rule that decides the order.

sections.heading: Two teams level on points
paragraphs: Article 9 of the Football Match Instruction defines the points system applied unless a competition statute provides otherwise. A win brings 3 points and a draw 1 point. The team with the most points stands first. The 2026-2027 Süper Lig statute does not write a separate order for goal difference. Article 9 of the Instruction is therefore in force.

If two teams are level on points, the order is as follows. First, the points advantage in the matches between the two teams is considered. If points are also level, the goal difference in those matches is considered. If goals scored in those matches are level, the team that scored more goals away is not counted as ahead. If points and goals between them are still level, the goal difference over the overall record is considered. If goal difference is also level, the team that has scored more goals is counted as ahead. If it is still level, the team without a forfeit defeat is counted as ahead. If it is still level after these, a single-match knockout-style match decides the winner under the stated principles.

sections.heading: Three or more teams level on points
paragraphs: If three or more teams are level on points, a points table is first drawn up from the matches the teams played against each other. The Instruction says that results of matches played between two or more teams level on points in this table are not looked at again. In the table, points are considered first, then goal difference if points are level, then goals scored if goal difference is level. If goals scored in these matches are level, away goals give no advantage.

If points, goals scored and goals conceded in the mini-table are also level, the process moves to the goal difference in the overall table. If overall goal difference is level, the team that has scored more goals in the overall record is counted as ahead. If it is still level, the team without a forfeit defeat is counted as ahead. If it is still level after these, a match or matches played under the principles set by the TFF decide the winner.

The third paragraph of Article 9 of the Instruction says that the TFF may decide not to apply goal difference, or to apply it differently, where it considers it necessary. The TFF's current Süper Lig points table page also ties to the Instruction that, once all matches the teams play against each other are completed, teams level on points will be ranked by the results between themselves.

faq.q: How many teams are relegated from the Süper Lig?
faq.a: Under the 2026-2027 statute, the three teams in 16th, 17th and 18th place go down to the TFF 1. Lig.

faq.q: What is looked at first when points are level?
faq.a: Article 9 of the Football Match Instruction looks first at the points advantage in the matches between the teams level on points.

faq.q: Do away goals break goal difference?
faq.a: The Instruction says that if goals scored in the matches between them are level, the team that scored more away goals is not counted as ahead.

faq.q: When does overall goal difference come in?
faq.a: When points and goals between two teams are still level. With three or more teams, when points, goals scored and goals conceded are also level in the mini-table between them.
